summary: Frontend-only end-to-end retest completed on the public preview at desktop 1920x1080 and mobile 390x844. All requested functional flows passed: repeated preloaders detached below 6s, SwiftShader correctly received the CSS orb with no canvas, hero copy rendered, every desktop/mobile nav target and footer back-to-top worked, masked About/Contact headings fully revealed, all four projects and images loaded, the skills marquee animated, and the contact form produced error/success toasts, cleared fields, and sent no mutation request. No console or page errors occurred. One reduced-motion accessibility defect and one minor contrast issue remain.

ui_bugs.issue: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulated, the app correctly avoids WebGL but the fallback orb still continuously translates and rotates. Its computed transform changed from matrix(0.985517, 0.00135118, -0.00135118, 0.985517, 0, -0.591209) to matrix(0.999914, 0.0130695, -0.0130695, 0.999914, 0, -5.5659) in 700ms.

issues: Placeholder color #5b5b64 on #0a0a0a is approximately 2.95:1 contrast, below the 4.5:1 guidance for the 18px regular-weight placeholder text.

action_items: Honor prefers-reduced-motion in HeroOrbFallback by disabling the infinite y/rotate animation, ideally via useReducedMotion or MotionConfig.
Increase contact placeholder contrast to at least 4.5:1.
Resolve the three repository ESLint errors in components/ui/calendar.jsx and components/ui/command.jsx before enforcing lint in CI.
critical_code_review_comments: hasHardwareGPU treats reduced motion as a fallback condition, but HeroOrbFallback unconditionally defines infinite y and rotate animation arrays; the preference changes the rendering technology without actually reducing motion.

Static analysis is not clean: ESLint reports two react/no-unstable-nested-components errors in calendar.jsx and one react/no-unknown-property error in command.jsx. These components were not exercised by this portfolio route.
seed_data_creation: None; the visual-only contact form sent no network mutation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend intentionally skipped. Current Chromium renderer was ANGLE/Vulkan SwiftShader. Fresh-load preloader samples were 3.115s desktop, 2.681s mobile, then 3.813s/5.170s/4.997s across three repeated desktop loads; all detached under 6s and rendered one CSS fallback with zero canvas elements. Desktop nav landed each target at ~90px, footer reached scrollY 0 in 2s, mobile links all changed scrollY and closed the menu, About/Contact transforms were all none on both viewports, all project images loaded at width 1400, and the marquee transform changed over 700ms. The initial desktop script used the marquee container rather than .rfm-marquee and produced a test-selector-only failure; the corrected selector passed and this is not an application defect.
rca_of_the_issue: Functional GPU fallback behavior is fixed: hasHardwareGPU identifies SwiftShader and Hero renders HeroOrbFallback instead of mounting Canvas, eliminating the prior headless WebGL starvation. The remaining reduced-motion defect is caused by selecting HeroOrbFallback for that preference while HeroOrbFallback itself always runs infinite Framer Motion y/rotate animations.
